plan: Store the input dictionary deep-copied in the Workspace and return deep copies from to_data(), so external mutation can never leak in or out.
Represent content as the recursive part-whole tree given by the data format: sections and groups carry an 'items' list, notes and references are leaves.

Implement one shared depth-first generator (_walk) yielding (item, depth) in list order; build total_word_count(), unresolved_markers(), and outline() on top of it so every operation applies uniformly at every nesting level.

For notes, strip marker tokens [[?identifier]] with a regex before counting words with \b\w+\b; the same marker regex harvests identifiers, merged with each reference's declared 'unresolved' list, deduplicated and sorted.
Render the outline deterministically: workspace title first, then '  ' * depth + '<kind>: <title>' per item in traversal order.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate item and destination, require the destination to be 'workspace' or a section/group, reject moving a container into itself or any descendant (subtree scan), and bounds-check the index against the destination — all before the single pop/insert, guaranteeing failed moves leave to_data() byte-identical.
mechanisms: uniform operations across levels via a single shared depth-first traversal
recursive aggregation for word totals and marker collection
deterministic pre-order traversal for outline rendering
containment invariant enforcement (container kinds only, no self/descendant destination)
atomic move: full validation before any mutation
